sentences.text: By the impugned order, the learned trial court in exercise of powers U/s 319 Cr.P.c. on an application of prosecution has summoned the revisionist-accused to face trial for offence U/s 302 IPC.

The first information report was lodged on 07.06.2014 by Radhey Shyam Pal (opposite party no.2)
alleging therein that he has solemnized the marriage of his sister Sarita with Surendra Pal on Vivekanand Pal @ Govind Pal vs State Of U.P. And Another on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163548611/
1 24.04.2012 and has given dowry and gifts according to his status.

sentences.text: Soon after marriage, her husband started demanding motorcycle and colour T.V. as additional dowry.
Due to non-fullfilment of demand of dowry Sarita was being harassed and tortured by her husband and mother in-law.
In the night i.e. 06.06.2014 about 12 O' clock

Saroj Devi informed on mobile phone that Sarita has received an electric shock and when the complainant reached at her in-laws house, they saw that his sister was lying in a burnt condition on the bed.
She has been murdered by her husband, mother-in-law and Nand (Arti).
After investigation, the charge-sheet was submitted against all the three named accused persons.

During the course of investigation, after examination of four witnesses, an application U/s 319 Cr.P.C. was filed by the prosecution alleging therein that in the cross examination of the witnesses the name of Vivekanand Pal alias Govind Pal has come into light and an offence U/s 302 IPC is made out against him.
The learned trial court by the impugned order has allowed the aforesaid application and has summoned Vivekanand Pal.

Learned counsel for the revisionist contended that applicant was not named in the FIR which was lodged against the husband, mother-in-law and Nand of the deceased with the allegations of demand of dowry and torture.
During the investigation, the Investigating Officer has recorded the statement of complainant and many other witnesses.

Even in the statement recorded U/s 161 Cr.P.C.
the name of the applicant-accused has not been disclosed and only the allegations of the FIR has been reiterated.
Even in the deposition before the court, the witnesses P.W.s-1 to 4 in their examination-in-chief has reiterated the version of the FIR and previous statement recorded U/s 161 Cr.P.C.

During cross-examination for the first time, it has come that revisionist-accused has illicit relations with the Nand of the deceased and due to this, he has committed the murder of the sister of the complainant.
This oral testimony is also based on hearsay.

Learned counsel further contended that powers U/s 319 Cr.P.C. is an extraordinary power and it should be exercised sparingly and with utmost care and caution and it requires standard of evidence which is more than that of prima-facie case.
It is also contended that trial of the co-accused named in the FIR has concluded and they have been acquitted.

Learned counsel placed reliance on the following case:
S. Mohammed Ispahani vs. Yogendra Chandak and ors, AIR 2017 SC 4994, Naveen vs. State of Haryana and ors, 2022 0 (SC) 1107, Sagar vs. State of U.P. and another 2022 0 SCC 217 Sunil Kumar Gupta and ors vs. State of U.P. & Khusbu Gupta vs.
State of U.P. and ors.
Learned AGA opposed the prayer.

sentences.text: The Apex Court in the case of Hardeep Singh Vs. State of Punjab AIR 2014 Supreme Court page 1400 has prescribed the standard of evidence required for exercising powers under section 319 Cr.P.C.

entities.text: Hardeep Singh Vs. State of Punjab AIR 2014 Supreme Court
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relevant paras 98 and 99 are as follows:
"98.
Power under Section 319, Cr.P.C. is a discretionary and an extra-ordinary power.
It is to be exercised sparingly and only in those cases where the circumstances of the case so warrant.
It is not to be exercised because the Magistrate or the Sessions Judge is of the opinion that some other person may also be guilty of committing that offence.

Only where strong and cogent evidence occurs against a person from the Vivekanand Pal @ Govind Pal vs State Of U.P. And Another on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163548611/
2 evidence led before the court that such power should be exercised and not in a casual and cavalier manner."
"99.

entities.text: Vivekanand Pal @ Govind Pal vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, we hold that though only a prima face case is to be established from the evidence led before the court not necessarily tested on the anvil of cross-examination,
it requires much stronger evidence than mere probability of his complicity,

The test that has to be applied is one which is more than prima facie case as exercised at the time of framing of charge, but short of satisfaction to an extent that the evidence, if goes unrebutted, would lead to conviction.
In the absence of such satisfaction, the court should refrain from exercising power under Section 319, Cr.P.C.

In Section 319,
Cr.P.C. the purpose of providing if 'it appears from the evidence that any person not being the accused has committed any offence is clear from the words "for which such person could be tried together with the accused."
The words used are not 'for which such person could be convicted'.
There is, therefore, no scope for the Court acting under Section 319, Cr.P.C, to form any opinion as to the guilt of the accused."
In the case of Brijendra Singh and others Vs. State of Rajasthan (2017) 7 SCC page 706 the Apex Court has reiterated the principles laid down in Hardeep Singh's case.

entities.text: Brijendra Singh and others Vs. State of Rajasthan (2017) 7 SCC page 706
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The relevant para no. 13 is quoted below:

"13. In order to answer the question, some of the principles enunciated in Hardeep Singh's case may be recapitulated: power under Section 319 Cr.P.C. can be exercised by the trial court at any stage during the trial, i.e., before the conclusion of trial, to summon any person as an accused and face the trial in the ongoing case, once the trial court finds that there is some ''evidence' against such a person on the basis of which evidence it can be gathered that he appears to be guilty of offence.
The ''evidence' herein means the material that is brought before the Court during trial.

Insofar as the material/evidence collected by the IO at the stage of inquiry is concerned, it can be utilised for corroboration and to support the evidence recorded by the Court to invoke the power under Section 319 Cr.P.C.

No doubt, such evidence that has surfaced in examination-in-chief, without cross- examination of witnesses,
can also be taken into consideration.

However, since it is a discretionary power given to the Court under Section 319 Cr.P.C. and is also an extraordinary one, same has to be exercised sparingly and only in those cases where the circumstances of the case so warrants.
The degree of satisfaction is more than the degree which is warranted at the time of framing of the charges against others in respect of whom charge-sheet was filed.
Only where strong and cogent evidence occurs against a person from the evidence led before the Court that such power should be exercised.
It is not to be exercised in a casual or a cavalier manner.
The prima facie opinion which is to be formed requires stronger evidence than mere probability of his complicity."
In this case, the revisionist-accused is not named in the FIR.
There is no allegations against him and the FIR has been lodged with the allegations that the deceased was harassed and tortured by her husband and in-laws.

The witnesses examined by the Investigating Officer, has also given the same Vivekanand Pal @ Govind Pal vs State Of U.P. And Another on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163548611/
3 statements as alleged in the FIR.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The name of the revisionist accused is not there in the statement recorded U/s 161 Cr.P.C.
Even in the examination-in-chief of the prosecution witnesses, the story as alleged in the FIR has been reiterated.
The named of accused revisionist has come for the first time in the cross examination of the witness with a different story.

Applying the test as prescribed by the Apex Court in a catena decision on the present set of facts it is clear that the learned trial court has failed to appreciate the entire facts, evidence and other material on record and has passed the impugned order in a cursory and mechanical manner.
In fact, there is no sufficient or cogent evidence against the revisionist on the basis of which he can be summoned in exercise of powers U/s 319 Cr.P.C.
So the impugned order suffers from material illegality and not sustainable in the eye of law.
Accordingly the revision is hereby allowed and the impugned order dated 10.05.2016 is set aside.
